classification.difficultyReason: Scaffolded coefficient comparison, amplitude and phase calculations lead to an exact equation solution and a related sketch.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $\sqrt{3}\cos x-\sin x=B\cos(x+\theta)$, show that $B\cos\theta=\sqrt{3}$ and $B\sin\theta=1$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}B\cos(x+\theta)&=B\cos x\cos\theta-B\sin x\sin\theta\end{aligned}$$
Comparing coefficients of $\cos x$ and $\sin x$:
$$\begin{aligned}B\cos\theta&=\sqrt{3}\\B\sin\theta&=1\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $B$, if $B>0$, by squaring and adding.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{B\sin\theta}{B\cos\theta}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$$
Since $B>0$, both $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ are positive, so $\theta$ is in quadrant I.
$$\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Solve the equation $\sqrt{3}\cos x-\sin x=1$, for $0\leq x\leq2\pi$.

children.label: e
children.prompt:
Sketch $y=\sqrt{3}\cos x-\sin x$, for $0\leq x\leq2\pi$.
On the same diagram, sketch the line $y=1$.
Indicate on your diagram the solutions of the equation in part d.

answer.worked:
$$y=2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$$
The curve has amplitude $2$ and period $2\pi$. It starts and ends at $y=\sqrt{3}$, has a minimum at $\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6},-2\right)$ and a maximum at $\left(\dfrac{11\pi}{6},2\right)$. The line $y=1$ intersects it at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

spec.description: Equation-driven sinusoidal graph with the source tick pattern and dashed horizontal line. Both requested intersections are explicitly marked and labelled. Ordinary axes and ticks use house black; the function and comparison line use standard blue, distinguished by solid and dashed strokes.
spec.mathematics: y=2 cos(x+pi/6), 0<=x<=2pi; y=1; intersections (pi/6,1) and (3pi/2,1); minimum (5pi/6,-2), maximum (11pi/6,2).
